candidates.classification: New bounded current source-derived operation case; actual authored rig and terrain reachability remain open.
candidates.trace: The pose buffer obtains an authored rig and sampled finite local pose, selects the named upper leg, lower leg and foot, and can conform a nonculled authored locomotion pose to terrain. It computes raw hip-to-knee and knee-to-ankle lengths before solve_pose_two_bone. For a zero-length upper segment and one-metre lower segment, the solver forms clamp bounds 1.0 + 0.0001 and 1.0 - 0.0001. Its prior target direction check does not validate segment lengths; an ordinary finite nonzero target direction passes the pinned glam Vec3 normalization contract. Rust f32::clamp panics for reversed bounds before the Option-returning solver can reject an invalid result.
candidates.symbolic_example: Assume an identity owner transform, selected canonical left leg with hip=(0,2,0), knee=(0,2,0), ankle=(0,1,0), weight one, no retained plant and a terrain target=(0,1.5,0). If the actual rig/terrain/animation admission and locomotion/culling guards permit that state, the half-metre foot displacement bypasses the identity no-op, target minus hip is (0,-0.5,0), and the two segment lengths are 0 and 1 metre. This is a symbolic source example, not an executed rig, GLB, terrain, float probe, animation or observed crash.
candidates.guards_and_limits: The selected clip/pose must exist, the actor must reach authored locomotion terrain conformity with an admitted terrain and sufficient IK weight, and the rig must not be culled or physics-owned. If the target is unchanged, the identity guard skips solving; a zero target vector exits through try_normalize. Actual base-rig asset, export path, skeletal proportions, terrain/support admission and whether a zero segment is supported or excluded remain unproved. No current player, visible glitch, panic occurrence or tactical gameplay effect is claimed.
candidates.related_059: ADLER-L11-POSE-LEG-ROLE-REDECODING is an earlier, separate question about case-folded anatomical role selection; its repair dependencies explicitly leave native two-bone minimum-length bounds open. A shared rig path does not make that role-identity first failure identical to this arithmetic panic.
candidates.connected_repair: Admit a valid complete two-segment solve range or return an explicit unavailable result before native clamp; make the choice at the real rig/pose and solver contract, preserving intended zero-target and no-op behavior and avoiding an undocumented compatibility fallback. Trace all callers and native asset policies before deciding how invalid authored rigs are reported.
candidates.later_acceptance: After separate implementation and product-validation authorization, cover valid ordinary chains, zero/tiny segment bounds, finite nonzero targets, unchanged target, and any project-required native animation diagnostics.
